source.title: A Control Theoretic Framework for Adaptive Gradient Optimizers in Machine Learning

record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers and SGD on natural image-classification and language-modeling tasks using training and held-out performance; it does not test random-label memorization or the other mapped interventions.
record.gate_note: The reported optimizer comparisons and training/test metrics bear on V4. The paper also reports moment-estimate traces for Adam and AdamSSM, but those do not measure a property named by the mapped versions. Results cited from prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: Independent optimizer comparisons measure training and test performance relevant to V4. The protocol differs from its limited-tuning condition: several methods also tune momentum, and AdamW additionally tunes weight decay. The proposed optimizer's performance alone is not a test of the mapped claims.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase captures the authors' claim that AdamSSM balances generalization and convergence speed through modified second-moment dynamics. It should not imply universal superiority: Adam wins test perplexity at one layer and AdaBelief at two layers. The convergence guarantees are asymptotic and continuous-time; a finite-time rate remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: Discrete-time Euler implementation of a newly proposed optimizer and comparisons with established optimizers; natural-label CIFAR-10 and Penn TreeBank tasks, with optimizer-specific hyperparameter selections and fixed epoch budgets.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome differs by optimizer, task, and LSTM depth. Image runs use 200 epochs and batch size 128; language runs use 200 epochs and batch size 20. Hyperparameter selection differs across algorithms.

fits_no_version.finding: AdamSSM has the highest reported best test accuracy on both image architectures, second-lowest test perplexity on the one- and two-layer LSTMs, and lowest on the three-layer LSTM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed second-moment modification improves benchmark performance under the selected training recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 6 shows less fluctuation in AdamSSM's second-moment estimates than Adam's for two selected VGG11 parameter coordinates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Modified second-moment dynamics can attenuate fluctuations in optimizer state; these traces do not establish a generalization mechanism.

record.peer_reviewed: at - Automatisierungstechnik (venue as provided); paper text also says preprint, under review
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the comparison tables. Only two image architectures and one language dataset are tested. The paper says hyperparameters are tuned for better test generalization but gives limited search details for some methods. Table 3–5 headings say 'Test accuracy' and 'Train accuracy' even though the text describes the language results as perplexity.
record.rows_left_out: No reported optimizer comparison rows omitted. Table 1–5 results are repeated as Tables 6–10 in the supplemental material; the repeated copies are not duplicated as separate rows.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

A controlled comparison tuning only learning rates and decay schedules; systematic expansion of tuning budgets; switching from Adam to SGD. AdamW is compared, but decoupling is not isolated from other hyperparameter differences.
Batch-size interventions, epoch-budget comparisons, and compensating recipe changes.
Dropout interventions and interactions with training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All table values are best observed training and test metrics selected separately over 200 epochs, generally at different epochs; they are not paired measurements from one checkpoint. Hyperparameters were explicitly selected using test performance, so these are test-selected results rather than untouched held-out evaluations. SGD uses momentum 0.9. Several adaptive methods tune beta1 as well as learning rate, and AdamW also tunes weight decay. No uncertainty estimates are supplied, so small numerical differences cannot establish reliable advantages or equivalence. Language-table accuracy headings are erroneous: the values are perplexities. No other claim version is tested. Reversed states indicate the direction relative to the adaptive-method disadvantage; Adam's language-model advantages support an exception already included in V4.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.

Broad hyperparameter tuning beyond the stated selections; the experiments cover only CIFAR-10 with ResNet34 and VGG11, and Penn TreeBank with 1-, 2-, and 3-layer LSTMs. They do not test the optimizer comparisons on other image or language benchmarks.
Batch-size comparisons and changes to the training recipe.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10: Adam on ResNet34 and VGG11; AdamW and RAdam on VGG11, under the paper's expanded tuning protocol
relationships.reason: R3 and R13 show Adam test deficits of 1.62 and 1.71 percentage points; R14 and R17 show deficits of 0.72 and 0.81. Training performance is better than SGD except for R13.
relationships.display_finding: The reported adaptive test-accuracy deficits relative to SGD, despite better training performance in some comparisons, remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10: AdamW, Fromage, MSVAG and RAdam on ResNet34; Fromage on VGG11
relationships.reason: R4–R7 and R15 show only 0.05–0.34 percentage-point deficits, much smaller than Adam's, without uncertainty estimates.
relationships.display_finding: Selected adaptive methods reportedly had small accuracy deficits relative to SGD, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10: AdaBelief, AdaBound and Yogi on both architectures; MSVAG on VGG11
relationships.reason: R1, R2, R9, R11, R12, R16 and R19 report higher test accuracy than SGD, demonstrating optimizer-dependent scope; advantages range from 0.07 to 1.30 percentage points.
relationships.display_finding: Other adaptive methods reportedly exceeded SGD accuracy, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Penn TreeBank: Adam on one- and two-layer LSTMs
relationships.reason: R23 and R32 report test perplexities of 84.28 versus 85.07 and 67.27 versus 67.42, supporting V4's explicit exception that Adam can outperform SGD on word-level language models.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower Adam test perplexity than SGD for both LSTM depths remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Penn TreeBank: AdaBelief at all depths; AdaBound at one and three layers; MSVAG at one layer
relationships.reason: R21, R22, R25, R30, R39 and R40 report lower test perplexity than SGD, so the adaptive-method disadvantage does not extend to these configurations.
relationships.display_finding: Selected adaptive configurations reportedly achieved lower test perplexity than SGD, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Penn TreeBank: AdamW, RAdam and Yogi at all depths; MSVAG at two and three layers
relationships.reason: R24, R26, R28, R33–R35, R37, R42–R44 and R46 show higher test perplexity than SGD; only R24 and R26 also show better training perplexity.
relationships.display_finding: The reported higher adaptive test perplexities than SGD, despite better training perplexity in two comparisons, remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Penn TreeBank: AdaBound at two layers and Adam at three layers
relationships.reason: R31 and R41 show small test-perplexity deficits of 0.11 and 0.51, without uncertainty estimates.
relationships.display_finding: AdaBound and Adam reportedly had small perplexity disadvantages, but these comparisons remain unverified and uncertainty was unreported.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10: AdamW versus Adam on both architectures
relationships.reason: R3–R4 and R13–R14 show AdamW improving test accuracy from 93.02 to 94.59 and from 88.40 to 89.39, consistent with partial recovery through decoupled weight decay; tuning differences prevent causal isolation.
relationships.display_finding: The reported AdamW accuracy improvements over Adam remain unverified, with tuning differences preventing causal isolation.

relationships.condition: Penn TreeBank: AdamW versus Adam at all three depths
relationships.reason: R23–R24, R32–R33 and R41–R42 show AdamW worsening test perplexity relative to Adam, so recovery through decoupled weight decay does not occur under these selected recipes.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW reportedly worsened perplexity relative to Adam at every depth, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
